title: Mau Movement in Samoa
summary: The Mau was a nonviolent Samoan movement against colonial rule, formed in Apia in 1926 under New Zealand's administration. Its crisis came on 28 December 1929, 'Black Saturday', when police fired on a Mau parade in Apia; Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III was among those killed. Sources differ on the total of Samoan dead.

uncertainty.note: Window covers formation (1926) to Black Saturday (28 December 1929); the movement itself continued afterwards. Commons Library traces earlier roots to 1908.

importance.justification: Major anticolonial movement in Samoa; Black Saturday is described as the worst incident in New Zealand's relationship with Samoa.

audience_note: Describes police shootings of unarmed demonstrators, with deaths.

reviewer_note: Death toll differs: NZHistory gives eight Samoans plus one NZ policeman (Tamasese mortally wounded); Commons says Tamasese and ten others; Commons also says 'Black Sunday'. Toll left out of numbers. Pin is Apia centre (proxy, Mapcarta).
